title: Late Breaking Results: An Efficient and Scalable Track Assignment with GPU Parallelism
problem: Track assignment in physical design (between global and detail routing) is compute-intensive; sequential algorithms are slow and limit design closure iteration times in large-scale chip designs.
motivation: GPU parallelism is underutilized in EDA workflows; track assignment parallelization can enable faster design iteration and closure.
method: GPU-accelerated parallel track assignment algorithm that exploits the independence and divisibility of track assignment tasks into fine-grained parallelizable units. Employs asynchronous parallelism strategy to partition computation of routing resources and track assignment; simultaneously considers global and local nets for improved routability estimation.
key_novelty: Asynchronous fine-grained task partitioning for track assignment that decouples routing resource computation from track assignment, enabling efficient GPU scheduling.
contributions: Improved routability via simultaneous global/local net consideration
Significant speedup compared to related work

metrics.other: Significant speedup over related work; improved routability estimation

limitations: Specific speedup numbers and baseline comparisons not quantified; scalability to state-of-art multi-billion-gate designs; memory bandwidth limitations not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated track assignment via asynchronous fine-grained parallelism
